about.intro: Khitma.net is an app that began in the precincts of the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque. It lets people read and complete the Quran together: create a group to complete the Quran, share out its juz among the members with ease, and follow the khitma’s progress in a way that is convenient and open to everyone in your group.
about.title: How to use
about.video: The following video (in Arabic) explains in detail how to use Khitma.net.
about.bless: May Allah accept your worship, and may He keep you in His care and protection.

aqsa.description: Khitma.net began at the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque, where its first lines of code were written, and today it is still developed from the surroundings of Jerusalem. Here we offer you a worldwide group khitma for the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque, praying to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to lift the injustice from it and from all the lands of the Muslims.

gCreate.placeholder: e.g. the first juz, or pages 1–10
gCreate.sameDesc: All members share the same task within a set period. For example, everyone reads the first juz on the first day, the second juz on the second day, and so on. In this kind of khitma the admin sets the task and the period freely: a group can read five pages a day (for children, say), or two or three juz a day, and so on.
gCreate.notSameDesc: In this khitma each member of the group recites one juz, so that together the group completes the whole Quran, for example to dedicate its reward to someone who has passed away. If the khitma is recurring, the app can give each member their next juz automatically and share a WhatsApp message with the status of every member’s juz.
gCreate.title: Khitma title
gCreate.name: Your name (the khitma’s admin)
gCreate.recurringYesDesc: For groups that complete the Quran together regularly, even if not at a fixed pace. If you already run a group khitma on WhatsApp, for example, a group on Khitma.net will make things much easier for you, in sha Allah.
gCreate.distr: Members join the group, then you start the khitma and the app shares out the pages of the mushaf equally among all members. This kind of khitma suits large groups best: if 60 people take part, for example, each one gets about ten pages, roughly half a juz.
gCreate.distrNo: In this khitma each member of the group recites one juz, so that together the group completes the whole Quran, for example to dedicate its reward to someone who has passed away.
gCreate.recurringNoDesc: For family khitmas for loved ones who have passed away (may Allah have mercy on them), in houses of condolence, or for khitmas on all kinds of occasions and activities.

home.intro: Khitma.net is an app that began in the precincts of the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque. It lets people read and complete the Quran together: create a group to complete the Quran, share out its juz among the members with ease, and follow the khitma’s progress in a way that is convenient and open to everyone in your group.
home.ayat: verses recited by members of Khitma.net groups
home.duaa: Be part of the great reward, in sha Allah — create your group now, and please remember us in your prayers.
home.maybe: And who knows, perhaps together we share in
home.more: good deeds or more. For “whoever reads a letter of the Book of Allah has a good deed for it, and a good deed is multiplied tenfold”, and Allah multiplies for whom He wills.
home.daymaDesc: An app that helps you keep up good deeds, for “the most beloved deed to Allah is the most regular and constant even if it were little” (Sahih al-Bukhari). Start with a small step you can keep, like one page of Quran a day, tie it to a fixed time such as after prayer, log it with a single tap, and invite your family to a private circle if you wish.
